request.spec:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows their cut total, and the sheet shows a cut total for everyone. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The server already worked out each member's cut of a pool, so this change is front-end only. No stored data, server code or audit records changed. The changes are in `src/main/frontend/features/people/PeopleList.tsx`:

- **Person's cut total (`person-cut-total`):** a new "Cut" column. It adds up the person's cut in every pool they belong to. A pool that shows no cut (because it isn't balanced or has no pot) adds nothing, so a person in no paying pools shows `0.00`.
- **Sheet's cut total (`rollup-cut-total`):** a new line under the open total that adds up every person's cut total. Two choices the request left open:
  - **Retired people count**, even when they are hidden from the list.
  - **Pools that are members of other pools are left out.** Their cut ends up with their own members, so counting it too would double it.

I also made one change the request didn't ask for, in `RetireControl.tsx`: retiring someone now refreshes the pools. A retired member's share counts as 0.00, which changes the pool's total and its cuts. Before, the pool figures (and so the new cut totals) stayed out of date until the sheet was re-loaded.
